title: Bij Albert Heijn: hoeveelheden en pinnen
summary: Quantities at the market (ons, pondje, kilo, bakje) and paying by card

blocks.title: Hoeveelheden bij de kraam
blocks.body: Dutch markets and delis still use old-fashioned units. **een ons** (100g) and **een pondje** (500g, literally 'a little pound') sit alongside the metric **kilo** — you'll hear all three at the cheese stall.

blocks.title: Pinnen: hoe je in Nederland betaalt
blocks.body: **Pinnen** (paying by card) is the default — many small shops barely handle cash anymore, and some refuse it outright. *Kunt u pinnen?* is worth having ready, though almost everywhere the answer is a slightly surprised 'obviously'.
blocks.callout: Cash (*contant*) is the exception now, not the rule.

blocks.title: Tap to hear the checkout words

pairs.note: Some snackbars and small shops in the Netherlands don't accept cash at all anymore.

blocks.explain: *een ons* = 100 grams. *een pondje* is the 500-gram one.

blocks.prompt: Type how you'd ask for 500 grams of strawberries.
blocks.explain: *Een pondje aardbeien, alstublieft* — *pondje* is the informal 500g unit.
